source: FHFA 2027 conforming loan limit release; HousingWire; NAHB

headline: Loan limits rise
to *$855,400*
slides.fig_caption: Rise in the baseline limit for 2027
slides.sub: That is $22,650 more than 2026, but a smaller bump than last year.

slides.label: new one-unit ceiling in *high-cost* counties
slides.body: That is 150% of the baseline. Higher limits apply where 115% of the local median home value exceeds the baseline.

slides.title: How much the limit *rose*
slides.note: The increase mirrors FHFA's house price index from Q3 2025 to Q3 2026. Limits go up in *all but 24 counties*.

slides.title: More room for *conforming*
slides.body: Buyers needing a loan between $832,750 and $855,400 can stay conforming instead of going jumbo in 2027. Some lenders already lend above the old limit, so loop in a loan officer early.
